- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

7	      across 3 runs from the same init (fixed tile ownership + ascending-k/t reduce).
8

10	runs a fresh eager optimizer + opt.step(); the reference is now the PURE-fp64 canonical
11	transcription (ref_<opt>_step in tests/hw/test_reference_parity.py) applied PER TENSOR on
12	the kernel's captured grad + zero-init state. bf16 STAYS the compute precision (the kernel
13	is unchanged); fp64 is only the ground-truth yardstick.
14	
15	WHY THIS SHAPE (not a full loss-trajectory-vs-eager oracle): the bf16 wgmma fwd+bwd
16	and the deterministic grad reduction are SHARED with the already-gated adamw TC cell
17	(decoder 13/13+5, vit 21/21, mamba 5/5 — grad parity vs the bf16-faithful oracle).
18	A converted cell changes ONLY the per-element tail (apply_optimizer<Opt>), which is
19	the 14/0-apply-parity math. So the cell-specific NEW surface is exactly the tail, and
20	the right gate is "did the kernel's tail apply the canonical update to the reduced
21	grad correctly" — which is (1). The grad itself is validated by the adamw gates +
22	the determinism check (2) proves no race was introduced by the tail swap.

24	The reference apply is the canonical fp64 math (transcribed from csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h
25	— the SAME single source the kernel's apply_optimizer<Opt> compiles from), run on the grad
26	the kernel returns (fused_train_step(return_grad=True)). bf16-TC kernel vs fp64 reference →
27	fp32-reorder tol (1e-4); the SAM 2nd-backward surfaces (sharpness/sam_dir) carry the bf16-
28	TC-vs-fp64 floor tol (3e-2 / 2.5e-2).

31	  PYTHONPATH=. python -m tests.hw.test_l3tc_tail_gate                 # all converted
32	  PYTHONPATH=. python -m tests.hw.test_l3tc_tail_gate --cell lion/decoder

156	    # We force rescale to a small nonzero value AFTER construction so mu = rescale·phi(g,
157	    # sharpness) is a real, checkable quantity. meta_hidden_dim=32 (the kernel's compile-time
158	    # kSgPhiHidden — the known prior 64-bug). lamb=1.0 (the production supergrok_lamb default).

162	                        alpha_init=c.get("supergrok_alpha", 0.98),

196	def _neuralgrok_canonical_mv(grad, opt_obj, step, p_before=None):
197	    """The (m, v, p_after) the NeuralGrok tail MUST produce, by the canonical header math.
198	
199	    Transcribes csrc/algorithms/neuralgrok.h (the SINGLE source the kernel's
200	    apply_optimizer<NeuralGrok> calls) — the gate's docstring defines its reference as
201	    exactly this header math:
202	        psi   = sum_j psi_W2[j] * relu(psi_W1[j]*|g| + psi_b1[j]) + psi_b2   (kPsiHidden=16)
203	        g_amp = (psi*alpha + beta) * g
204	        m     = beta1*m_prev + (1-beta1)*g_amp        (m_prev = 0 at step 1, zero-init cache)
205	        v     = beta2*v_prev + (1-beta2)*g_amp^2
206	        update= (m/bc1) / (sqrt(v/bc2) + eps);  p_after = p - lr*(update + wd*p)   (AdamW tail)
207	    computed in fp64 on the SAME captured TC-reduced grad and the SAME psi weights the
208	    kernel read (opt_obj.psi_pack). Returns flat fp32 (m, v, p_after) for the whole param
209	    vector; p_after is None when p_before is None (the (1b)-only call shape).
210	
211	    RE-ANCHOR (task #10): the eager per-op neuralgrok_fused_step CUDA kernel is being
212	    DELETED, so BOTH (1a) params and (1b) m/v are now anchored to THIS ground-truth fp64
213	    transcription of neuralgrok.h — the same single source the kernel's apply_optimizer<
214	    NeuralGrok> compiles from. The kernel matches this canonical math to ~2.7e-7. (1a) used
215	    to compare the live eager opt.step(); with the eager path gone, the AdamW tail here IS
216	    the (1a) reference. bf16 stays the compute precision; fp64 is the yardstick.
217	    """
218	    dev = grad.device
219	    g64 = grad.double()
220	    # GLOBAL grad-norm clip — neuralgrok.h's tail clips the reduced grad (kernel P2.5,
221	    # st.clip_coef) BEFORE psi+amp. Apply the SAME clip to the reference so it tracks the
222	    # kernel when the clip FIRES (global grad-norm > grad_clip, e.g. seed 7); inert
223	    # (coef=1) when norm<=clip. total_norm = sqrt(Σ g²) over the reduced grad == the
224	    # kernel's P2.5 norm.
225	    _gclip = float(opt_obj.param_groups[0].get("grad_clip", 0.0))
226	    if _gclip > 0.0:
227	        _tn = g64.norm().item()
228	        if _tn > _gclip:
229	            g64 = g64 * (_gclip / (_tn + 1e-6))
230	    ag = g64.abs()
231	    pack = opt_obj.psi_pack(device=dev).double()
232	    H = (pack.numel() - 1) // 3
233	    W1 = pack[0:H]; b1 = pack[H:2 * H]; W2 = pack[2 * H:3 * H]; b2 = pack[3 * H]
234	    # psi = sum_j W2[j]*relu(W1[j]*|g| + b1[j]) + b2  (per element)
235	    hid = torch.relu(ag.unsqueeze(1) * W1.reshape(1, H) + b1.reshape(1, H))   # [N,H]
236	    psi = (hid * W2.reshape(1, H)).sum(1) + b2                                # [N]
237	    grp = opt_obj.param_groups[0]
238	    alpha = float(grp["alpha"]); beta = float(grp["beta"])
239	    beta1, beta2 = float(grp["betas"][0]), float(grp["betas"][1])
240	    g_amp = (psi * alpha + beta) * g64
241	    # step 1 from zero-init moments (the kernel's state cache zero-inits [m|v|extra]).
242	    m = (1.0 - beta1) * g_amp
243	    v = (1.0 - beta2) * g_amp * g_amp
244	    p_after = None
245	    if p_before is not None:
246	        # AdamW tail (the (1a) reference). bc1=1-β1, bc2=1-β2 at t=1.
247	        lr = float(grp.get("lr", 1e-3)); eps = float(grp.get("eps", 1e-8))
248	        wd = float(grp.get("weight_decay", 0.0))
249	        bc1 = 1.0 - beta1; bc2 = 1.0 - beta2
250	        pb = p_before.double().to(dev)
251	        update = (m / bc1) / (torch.sqrt(v / bc2) + eps)
252	        p_after = (pb - lr * (update + wd * pb)).float()
253	    return m.float(), v.float(), p_after

256	def _neuralgrok_factory(g, params, c):
257	    # train_neuralgrok: NeuralGrok(lr, betas, weight_decay, alpha=neural_alpha,
258	    #                              beta=neural_beta, num_layers=neural_layers,
259	    #                              hidden_dim=neural_hidden, grad_clip=neural_grad_clip).
260	    # PARITY PINS (the kernel's compile-time psi contract — OPTIMIZER_CONFIGS sets
261	    # these too): num_layers=2 and hidden_dim=16 == kPsiHidden, so the trained MLP IS
262	    # the deployed MLP (psi_pack maps it 1:1 into the kernel's `extra` slice). grad_clip
263	    # is forwarded from the config (default 1.0, == train_neuralgrok); the kernel's P2.5
264	    # clip applies it, and the canonical fp64 reference (_neuralgrok_canonical_mv) applies
265	    # the SAME clip — so the parity is real at any seed (inert when ‖g‖₂≤grad_clip).
266	    params = list(params)
267	    opt = g.NeuralGrok(params, lr=c["lr"], betas=(c["beta1"], c["beta2"]),
268	                       weight_decay=c["weight_decay"],
269	                       alpha=c.get("neural_alpha", 10.0),
270	                       beta=c.get("neural_beta", 4.0),
271	                       num_layers=c.get("neural_layers", 2),
272	                       hidden_dim=c.get("neural_hidden", 16),
273	                       grad_clip=c.get("neural_grad_clip", 1.0))
274	    # The amplifier is constructed on CPU in __init__; the race moves it to the
275	    # param device (grokking_race_v2.py:1094 opt.amplifier=opt.amplifier.to(dev)).
276	    # Mirror that — without it get_weights()/psi_pack() return CPU tensors, and the
277	    # kernel reads the psi `extra` slice from the wrong device. This is the production
278	    # device placement, not a test crutch.
279	    if params:
280	        opt.amplifier = opt.amplifier.to(params[0].device)
281	    return opt

551	def _build_cell(model, seed=int(os.environ.get("GATE_SEED", "42"))):
552	    """Build the live race model + one real batch + the L3-REAL flat layout.
553	
554	    DETERMINISM (load-bearing for gate 2): build_model does NOT reseed from
555	    c["seed"] internally — it draws from the global RNG — so the A/A/A determinism
556	    check MUST reseed here, or each rebuild yields different random init weights and
557	    the gate would compare runs with DIFFERENT inputs (a test bug, not kernel
558	    non-determinism). We torch.manual_seed(seed) immediately before build_model so
559	    every _build_cell(model, seed) returns byte-identical initial params."""
560	    g = _g()
561	    c = dict(g.DEFAULT_CONFIG)
562	    c.update({"model_type": model, "use_amp": False, "use_fused": True,
563	              "compile_model": False, "matmul_precision": "bf16", "seed": seed,
564	              "frac_train": 0.5, "val_ratio": 0.10, "p": 97})
565	    dev = torch.device("cuda")
566	    data = tuple(d.to(dev) for d in g.make_data_for_task(c, seed))
567	    torch.manual_seed(seed)            # pin build_model's global-RNG draw
568	    torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)
569	    m = g.build_model(c, dev)
570	    return g, c, m, data, dev

573	def _sg_bf16_sharpness_oracle(model, named_ref, tx, ty, grad, rho, total, dev):
574	    """The (g_sam − g)² sharpness the SAM 2nd backward MUST produce, via the bf16-FAITHFUL
575	    fp64 oracle (the SAME instrument the looksam sam_dir check + the first-grad gate use).
576	    Runs the oracle TWICE — at p and at p'=p+ron·g (ron=rho/‖g‖_global, g the kernel's reduced
577	    grad) — and returns sharpness_bf = (g_sam_bf − g_bf)² flattened (named layout order). The
578	    bf16-TC kernel 2nd backward vs this fp64-bf16-faithful 2nd backward differ only by the bf16
579	    floor (the SAME design floor the looksam sam_dir 2e-2 tol calibrates), so sharpness is
580	    checked at that floor. A SKIPPED SAM phase (sharpness≈0) fails the liveness assert."""
581	    if model == "decoder":
582	        from tests.hw.test_decoder_tc import _bf16_faithful_oracle as _orc
583	        B = int(tx.shape[0]); B16 = B - (B % 16)
584	        a0 = tx[:B16].to(torch.long); a1 = ty[:B16].to(torch.long)
585	        named_d = {n: p.detach() for n, p in named_ref}
586	        _lo, go = _orc(named_d, a0, a1)
587	    elif model == "mamba":
588	        # The mamba twin of the decoder branch: int tokens, the bf16-faithful fp64 mamba
589	        # oracle (the SAME instrument the looksam/mamba sam_dir check + the first-grad gate
590	        # use). B%16 truncation matches fused_train_step's wgmma path.
591	        from tests.hw.test_mamba_tc import _bf16_faithful_mamba_oracle as _orc
592	        B = int(tx.shape[0]); B16 = B - (B % 16)
593	        a0 = tx[:B16].to(torch.long); a1 = ty[:B16].to(torch.long)
594	        named_d = {n: p.detach() for n, p in named_ref}
595	        _lo, go = _orc(named_d, a0, a1)
596	    elif model == "vit":
597	        from tests.hw.test_vit_tc import _bf16_faithful_oracle as _orc
598	        B = int(tx.shape[0]); B16 = B - (B % 16)
599	        a0 = tx[:B16].detach().cpu().double(); a1 = ty[:B16].detach().cpu().to(torch.long)
600	        named_d = {n: p.detach().cpu() for n, p in named_ref}
601	        _lo, go = _orc(named_d, a0, a1)
602	    else:
603	        raise NotImplementedError(f"sg sharpness oracle not wired for {model}")
604	    gn = torch.sqrt(sum((gv.double() ** 2).sum() for gv in go.values())).item()
605	    ron = rho / gn
606	    off = 0; named_pert = {}
607	    cpu = (model == "vit")
608	    for n_, p in named_ref:
609	        k = p.numel()
610	        base = (p.detach().cpu().double() if cpu else p.detach().double())
611	        gslice = grad[off:off + k].reshape(p.shape)
612	        gslice = (gslice.cpu().double() if cpu else gslice.double())
613	        named_pert[n_] = base + ron * gslice
614	        off += k
615	    _lo2, go2 = _orc(named_pert, a0, a1)
616	    sharp = torch.cat([((go2[n_] - go[n_]).reshape(-1).double()) ** 2
617	                       for n_, _ in named_ref]).float().to(dev)
618	    return sharp

1	"""Runtime hardware detection for the fused kernel architecture.
2	
3	Detection is **arch-honest**: ``detect_arch()`` / ``get_gpu_arch()`` report the
4	REAL device architecture, not a collapsed vendor selector. An A100 reports
5	``sm_80``, an L40S ``sm_89``, an H100 ``sm_90a`` — they are NOT all flattened to
6	``90``. AMD reports its real ``gfx<...>`` target; TPU reports ``tpu_v6e``.
7	
8	    NVIDIA: sm_70 / sm_75 / sm_80 / sm_86 / sm_89 / sm_90a / sm_100a / ...
9	    AMD:    gfx906 / gfx908 / gfx90a / gfx942 / gfx950 / gfx110x / ...
10	    TPU:    tpu_v6e

13	vendor family; see setup.py), so the *fat-binary impl selector* is a separate
14	concern from the reported arch. ``normalize_arch()`` maps a real arch to its
15	impl-family selector (NVIDIA → 90, AMD → 942, TPU → "tpu_v6e") for the code
16	paths that load the matching per-SM/-gfx code from the fat binary. Reporting
17	stays honest; only the binary loader normalises.

19	Feature predicates (``supports_fp8`` etc.) are keyed to the REAL compute
20	capability via ``get_device_sm()``. ``FORCE_ARCH`` accepts any real arch form
21	(``sm_80``, ``gfx942``, ``tpu_v6e``, or a bare numeric CC like ``80``/``90``).

188	def _sm_to_arch_label(cc: int) -> str:
189	    """Map a real NVIDIA compute capability int to its canonical arch label.
190	
191	    Honest: an A100 (CC 80) → ``sm_80``, an L40S (CC 89) → ``sm_89``, an H100
192	    (CC 90) → ``sm_90a``. A CC above the highest known entry resolves to that
193	    highest label (forward-compatible), a CC below the lowest raises.
194	    """
195	    label = None
196	    for threshold, name in _NVIDIA_CC_LABELS:
197	        if cc >= threshold:
198	            label = name
199	    if label is None:
200	        raise UnsupportedArchError(
201	            f"NVIDIA compute capability {cc} is below the minimum supported "
202	            f"(sm_70).")
203	    return label

206	def _normalize_force_arch(force: str) -> Union[int, str]:
207	    """Map a FORCE_ARCH string to the REAL arch it names (honest).
208	
209	    Returns a real arch label (``sm_80``/``gfx942``/...) or ``tpu_v6e``. A bare
210	    numeric value is treated as an NVIDIA compute capability and resolved to its
211	    real label. Raises on unrecognised input. Use :func:`normalize_arch` on the
212	    result when an impl-family selector (90/942) is needed.
213	    """
214	    if force.startswith('tpu'):
215	        return "tpu_v6e"
216	    # AMD: any gfx target. Honor the exact gfx label; the bare ``942`` form maps
217	    # to gfx942 for back-compat.
218	    if force.startswith('gfx'):
219	        return force
220	    if force == '942':
221	        return "gfx942"
222	    # NVIDIA: sm_* label (normalise the bare ``sm_90`` alias to ``sm_90a`` etc.)
223	    if force.startswith('sm_'):
224	        try:
225	            cc = int(force[3:].rstrip('a'))
226	        except ValueError:
227	            raise UnsupportedArchError(
228	                f"FORCE_ARCH={force!r} not recognized.") from None
229	        return _sm_to_arch_label(cc)
230	    if force.startswith('sm'):
231	        try:
232	            cc = int(force[2:].rstrip('a'))
233	        except ValueError:
234	            raise UnsupportedArchError(
235	                f"FORCE_ARCH={force!r} not recognized.") from None
236	        return _sm_to_arch_label(cc)
237	    # Bare numeric compute capability (e.g. ``80`` for A100, ``90`` for H100).
238	    if force.isdigit():
239	        return _sm_to_arch_label(int(force))
240	    raise UnsupportedArchError(
241	        f"FORCE_ARCH={force!r} not recognized. Use an NVIDIA arch "
242	        f"(sm_70..sm_120a or a numeric CC), an AMD arch (gfx906..gfx1201), "
243	        f"or tpu_v6e.")

246	def normalize_arch(arch: Union[int, str]) -> Union[int, str]:
247	    """Map a real arch to its fat-binary impl-family selector.
248	
249	    NVIDIA labels (``sm_*``) and bare CC ints → ``90``; AMD ``gfx*`` (and the
250	    bare ``942``) → ``942``; ``tpu_v6e`` → ``"tpu_v6e"``. This is the ONLY place
251	    the NVIDIA→90 / AMD→942 collapse happens, and it is used solely by the code
252	    that loads the matching per-arch code from the multi-arch fat binary — never
253	    for *reporting* the device's real arch.
254	    """
255	    if arch == "tpu_v6e":
256	        return "tpu_v6e"
257	    if isinstance(arch, int):
258	        return 942 if arch == 942 else 90
259	    if arch.startswith('gfx'):
260	        return 942
261	    if arch.startswith('sm'):
262	        return 90
263	    raise UnsupportedArchError(f"Cannot normalize unknown arch {arch!r}")

332	@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=1)
333	def detect_arch() -> Union[int, str]:
334	    """Detect the active REAL arch: a label like ``sm_80`` / ``sm_90a`` /
335	    ``gfx942``, or ``"tpu_v6e"``.
336	
337	    Detection order:
338	      1. FORCE_ARCH env var (accepts sm_*, gfx*, a numeric CC, or tpu_v6e)
339	      2. TPU detection via JAX
340	      3. GPU detection via get_gpu_arch()
341	
342	    The result is the device's honest arch — an A100 reports ``sm_80``, never a
343	    collapsed ``90``. Apply :func:`normalize_arch` for the fat-binary impl
344	    selector. Raises ``UnsupportedArchError`` if no supported arch is found.
345	    """
346	    force = os.environ.get('FORCE_ARCH')
347	    if force:
348	        return _normalize_force_arch(force)
349	
350	    # Try TPU detection first (check if JAX is available and running on TPU)
351	    try:
352	        import jax  # noqa: F401
353	        import jax.devices
354	        devices = jax.devices()
355	        if devices and any(d.platform == 'tpu' for d in devices):
356	            return "tpu_v6e"

361	    arch = get_gpu_arch()

451	# C++ extension loader (consolidated from _ops_loader.py).
452	# Loads the per-arch specialized C++ extension. Raises on first kernel
453	# attribute access if the extension isn't built — there is no Python
454	# fallback path, but `import grokking_optimizers` succeeds either way so
455	# that profiling / tooling code can introspect the package without a

460	class _LazyOps:
461	    """Lazy proxy for the compiled `grokking_optimizers._ops` extension.
462	
463	    Resolves on first attribute access. `hasattr(_ops, "foo")` correctly
464	    returns False when the extension isn't built; direct attribute access
465	    raises AttributeError with a descriptive build hint. This preserves the
466	    no-fallback contract (kernels are unreachable without a build) while
467	    allowing import-time introspection.
468	    """
469	    __slots__ = ("_real", "_error", "_attr_cache")
470	
471	    def __init__(self):
472	        object.__setattr__(self, "_real", None)
473	        object.__setattr__(self, "_error", None)
474	        # Memoize resolved kernel attributes so repeated `_ops.fn` access on
475	        # the hot path skips the module getattr after the first lookup.
476	        object.__setattr__(self, "_attr_cache", {})
477	
478	    def _resolve(self):
479	        if self._real is not None:
480	            return self._real
481	        if self._error is not None:
482	            return None  # cached failure
483	        try:
484	            import importlib
485	            real = importlib.import_module("grokking_optimizers._ops")
486	            object.__setattr__(self, "_real", real)
487	            return real
488	        except ImportError as e:
489	            object.__setattr__(self, "_error", e)
490	            logger.debug("grokking_optimizers._ops not importable "
491	                         "(extension unbuilt?): %s", e)
492	            return None
493	
494	    def __getattr__(self, name):
495	        if name.startswith("_"):
496	            raise AttributeError(name)
497	        cache = self._attr_cache
498	        cached = cache.get(name)
499	        if cached is not None:
500	            return cached
501	        real = self._resolve()
502	        if real is None:
503	            raise AttributeError(
504	                f"grokking_optimizers._ops.{name}: C++ extension not built. "
505	                f"Run `pip install -e .` (supported arches: {SUPPORTED_ARCHES}). "
506	                f"Original ImportError: {self._error}"
507	            )
508	        attr = getattr(real, name)
509	        cache[name] = attr
510	        return attr
511	
512	    def bind(self, name):
513	        """Resolve ``name`` once and return the underlying kernel callable.
514	
515	        Callers (optimizers) cache the returned bound function on the instance
516	        so subsequent steps skip the proxy ``__getattr__`` entirely. Raises the
517	        same descriptive error as attribute access if the extension is unbuilt.
518	        """
519	        return self.__getattr__(name)
520	
521	    def __bool__(self):
522	        return self._resolve() is not None
523	
524	    def __repr__(self):
525	        real = self._resolve()
526	        if real is None:
527	            return f"<_LazyOps unbuilt: {self._error}>"
528	        return f"<_LazyOps wrapping {real!r}>"
529	
530	
531	_cached_ops = _LazyOps()
532	
533	
534	def get_ops():
535	    """Return the lazy `_ops` proxy. Never raises at call time."""
536	    return _cached_ops

551	def has_kernels() -> bool:
552	    """True iff the compiled C++/CUDA/HIP kernel extension is importable AND
553	    exposes the fused optimizer kernels.
554	
555	    This is the honest capability flag (spec §6a): the optimizers have NO
556	    pure-PyTorch fallback for ``.step()`` — they hard-require this extension and

400	// Per-(device, n) reusable scratch for fused_step. The barrier counters and the
401	// `acts` proxy were previously reallocated (and `acts` memset over the full
402	// param size) on EVERY dispatch; sizes/offsets are constant for a given n.
403	// We persist them keyed by (device_index, n) and only reset the mutable parts
404	// (zero the 3 barrier counters + the acts buffer) per step. Behavior is
405	// identical — same zero-initialized scratch handed to the launcher — but the
406	// allocations/the full-size memset of sizes/offsets happen once per shape.
407	struct FusedScratch {
408	 torch::Tensor g_next;       // int32 [1]
409	 torch::Tensor g_arrived;    // int32 [1] (reinterpreted as unsigned)
410	 torch::Tensor g_generation; // int32 [1] (reinterpreted as unsigned)
411	 torch::Tensor sizes;        // int32 [1] = n  (constant per n)
412	 torch::Tensor offsets;      // int32 [1] = 0  (constant)
413	 torch::Tensor acts;         // float [numel(params)] proxy buffer
414	};
415	
416	// Keyed by (device_index, n). n disambiguates differing param shapes on the
417	// same device; acts is sized to params.numel() (== n here, single flat tensor).
418	inline FusedScratch& fused_scratch_for(const torch::Tensor& params, int64_t n) {
419	 static std::unordered_map<long long, FusedScratch> cache;
420	 const long long dev_idx =
421	 params.device().is_cuda() ? static_cast<long long>(params.device().index())
422	 : -1LL;
423	 const long long key = (dev_idx << 40) ^ static_cast<long long>(n);
424	 auto it = cache.find(key);
425	 if (it == cache.end()) {
426	 auto opts_i =
427	 torch::TensorOptions().device(params.device()).dtype(torch::kInt32);
428	 FusedScratch s;
429	 s.g_next = torch::zeros({1}, opts_i);
430	 s.g_arrived = torch::zeros({1}, opts_i);
431	 s.g_generation = torch::zeros({1}, opts_i);
432	 s.sizes = torch::full({1}, n, opts_i); // constant for this n
433	 s.offsets = torch::zeros({1}, opts_i); // constant
434	 s.acts = torch::zeros_like(params);
435	 it = cache.emplace(key, std::move(s)).first;
436	 } else {
437	 // Reset only the mutable scratch; sizes/offsets are invariant for this n.
438	 it->second.g_next.zero_();
439	 it->second.g_arrived.zero_();
440	 it->second.g_generation.zero_();
441	 it->second.acts.zero_();
442	 }
443	 return it->second;
444	}

580	// OptId int for the in-kernel optimizer TAIL, MIRRORING
581	// csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_components.cuh::OptId (kept as a local int map so this TU
582	// stays free of the device header — same discipline as the FusedScalars mirror).
583	// Returns the OptId for a SINGLE-LAUNCH wgmma-capable tail (no precompute stage, no
584	// 2nd backward, no sharpness ABI), or -1 for an optimizer whose L3-TC path needs more
585	// than the fwd+bwd+tail single launch (SG11/SG15/SG2). LookSAM IS now wired: its SAM
586	// 2nd backward is an IN-KERNEL phase (P2.4) — a perturb→2nd fwd+bwd→sam_dir=g_sam−g
587	// loop between B2 and P3, gated to every-k SAM steps — so it remains a SINGLE
588	// persistent launch (the same shape as Prodigy's P2.6 / Muon's P2.7 in-kernel stages).
589	// The owner-baseline directive routes exactly the -1!=... set onto the TC driver; the
590	// rest FAIL LOUD (here / in the Python gate) with their cited blocker.
591	static int wgmma_tail_opt_id(const std::string& optimizer) {
592	    if (optimizer == "adamw")      return 0;   // OptId::AdamW
593	    if (optimizer == "lion")       return 1;   // OptId::Lion
594	    if (optimizer == "grokfast")   return 2;   // OptId::Grokfast
595	    if (optimizer == "grokadamw")  return 3;   // OptId::GrokAdamW
596	    if (optimizer == "looksam")    return 4;   // OptId::LookSAM (MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd
597	                                               // backward — in-kernel P2.4 perturb→2nd
598	                                               // fwd+bwd→sam_dir, SINGLE persistent launch)
599	    if (optimizer == "prodigy")    return 5;   // OptId::Prodigy (STAGED global-d,
600	                                               // in-kernel P2.6 reduction — still a
601	                                               // SINGLE persistent launch)
602	    if (optimizer == "neuralgrok") return 6;   // OptId::NeuralGrok
603	    if (optimizer == "muon")       return 7;   // OptId::Muon (STAGED grid-cooperative
604	                                               // Newton-Schulz — in-kernel P2.7, still a
605	                                               // SINGLE persistent launch; vit wired)
606	    if (optimizer == "supergrok11") return 8;  // OptId::SuperGrok11 (MODEL-COUPLED SAM 2nd
607	                                               // backward → sharpness=(g_sam−g)² in P2.4 +
608	                                               // per-tensor meta-net mu/gate precompute in
609	                                               // P2.45; SINGLE persistent launch)
610	    if (optimizer == "supergrok15") return 9;  // OptId::SuperGrok15 (same SAM 2nd backward +
611	                                               // per-tensor mu precompute; gate is a host
612	                                               // scalar — SINGLE persistent launch)
613	    if (optimizer == "supergrok2")  return 10; // OptId::SuperGrok2 (FULL CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU
614	                                               // meta-net as the optimizer phase: in-kernel
615	                                               // SEGMENTED SORT (STAGE -1) + SAM 2nd backward
616	                                               // → sharpness + sg2_meta_stages; routed via the
617	                                               // DEDICATED mega_*_sg2_tc entry, NOT the generic
618	                                               // single-launch tail switch). Decoder/vit only;
619	                                               // mamba stays -1 (code-absent + A/A/A race).
620	    return -1;                                 // unroutable on the single-launch TC path
621	}

733	 // the EXISTING fused_step arity (the pybind py::arg list pins it) by reading
734	 // tokens/targets from the int32-reinterpreted `input` tensor:
735	 //   input = int32 [B*(kSeq+1)]  (first B*kSeq tokens row-major, last B targets)
736	 // and `state` = float [3*total + 1] ([m|v|extra] + a trailing loss slot the
737	 // kernel writes the mean loss into, which the Python wrapper reads back). The
738	 // workspace (nCTA*total grad partials + nCTA loss partials) is device scratch

740	 // (kSeq/kVocab/kD); B is derived from input.numel(). This leaves the 33
741	 // generated surrogate cells untouched (their surrogate-L3 path is now
742	 // unreachable dead code; see BUILD_AND_VALIDATE.md PHASE-1).

744	 // decoder real fwd+bwd+opt TC megakernel fires for the single-launch optimizer
745	 // tails (adamw/lion/grokfast/grokadamw/neuralgrok — wgmma_tail_opt_id >= 0). The
746	 // STAGED/coupled optimizers (wgmma_tail_opt_id < 0) and SuperGrok2 do not reach
747	 // here. (want_wgmma is always true now — the scalar path is removed.)
748	 const int dec_opt_id = wgmma_tail_opt_id(optimizer);

750	 // meta-net weight bundle + per-tensor scalar arrays this generic block cannot carry),
751	 // so EXCLUDE it here even though wgmma_tail_opt_id("supergrok2")==10.
752	 const bool dec_l3_real = ((optimizer == "adamw")
753	                          || (want_wgmma && dec_opt_id >= 0))
754	                          && optimizer != "supergrok2";
755	 if (arch == 90 && model == "transformer_decoder" && dec_l3_real && !opt_only) {
756	 const int64_t total = kDecoderTotalElems;
757	 TORCH_CHECK(params.numel() == total,
758	 "fused decoder megakernel: params has ", params.numel(),
759	 " elements but the small decoder has ", total,
760	 ". Pass the flat concat of named_parameters() in order.");
761	 TORCH_CHECK(params.scalar_type() == torch::kFloat32 && params.is_contiguous(),
762	 "fused decoder megakernel: params must be contiguous fp32.");
763	 // input = int32 tokens(B*kSeq) ++ targets(B). B = numel/(kSeq+1).
764	 TORCH_CHECK(input.scalar_type() == torch::kInt32 && input.is_contiguous(),
765	 "fused decoder megakernel: input must be contiguous int32 "
766	 "(packed tokens[B*kSeq]++targets[B]).");
767	 const int64_t in_n = input.numel();
768	 TORCH_CHECK(in_n % (kDecoderSeq + 1) == 0 && in_n > 0,
769	 "fused decoder megakernel: input.numel() (", in_n,
770	 ") must be B*(kSeq+1) = B*", kDecoderSeq + 1, ".");

773	 // LARGER buffer: [m|v|extra/s_track | loss | param_init(total) | r_ema|s_ema|d_lr]

775	 // estimator scalars after it). SuperGrok11/15 (meta-net mu + SAM 2nd backward) need
776	 // [m|v|mu | loss | sharpness(total) | phi_pack(4*32+1)] = 4*total + 1 + kSgPhiPack
777	 // (the TC launcher carves sharpness at loss_slot+1 and the phi pack after it). The
778	 // host (fused_train_step) sizes it per-cell.
779	 const bool is_sg = (optimizer == "supergrok11" || optimizer == "supergrok15");
780	 const int64_t min_state = (optimizer == "prodigy") ? (4 * total + 4)
781	                         : is_sg ? (4 * total + 1 + (int64_t)(4 * 32 + 1))
782	                         : (3 * total + 1);

786	 " elements (", (optimizer == "prodigy")

788	 : is_sg ? "[m|v|mu|loss|sharpness|phi_pack] for SuperGrok11/15"
789	 : "[m|v|extra]+loss", ").");

1	"""End-to-end verification harness — the single authoritative gate for
2	SuperGrok1.5.  "Know EVERYTHING; prove it works, and works *maximally*."
3	
4	This is the end-all-be-all.  It does not just check that individual files
5	compile in isolation — it proves that the **modular composition** works: every
6	optimizer compiles *together with* every model into the fused megakernel cell
7	for every arch (99 cells), and that each composition runs at its **maximal**
8	fusion tier.  It then cross-validates the generated artifacts against their
9	single source of truth so nothing can silently drift.
10	
11	It is organized as ordered phases; each phase prints one PASS/FAIL line per
12	check and accumulates into a final structured report.  Phases that need a tool
13	absent on this host (nvcc / clang / jax) are reported as SKIPPED-silicon rather
14	than silently passing.
15	
16	    PHASE 0  toolchain probe            — what can be proven here vs on silicon
17	    PHASE 1  structural inventory       — every component + 99 cells exist
18	    PHASE 2  single-component gates      — per-op launchers + models + headers
19	    PHASE 3  MODULAR COMPOSITION         — 99 cells: optimizer × model compile
20	                                            *together* (the core guarantee)
21	    PHASE 4  MAXIMALITY                   — max fusion tier, codegen idempotency,
22	                                            register/smem budget, math drift
23	    PHASE 5  cross-validation            — dispatch tables, self-test, ruff
24	    PHASE 6  report                       — totals + tier map + silicon + design
25	
26	Run:
27	    PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m grokking_optimizers.verify_all              # all
28	    PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m grokking_optimizers.verify_all --phase 3    # one
29	    PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m grokking_optimizers.verify_all --quick      # no compiles
30	    PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m grokking_optimizers.verify_all --jobs 8     # parallelism
31	
32	Failure policy mirrors utilization.py: a missing *expected* artifact or a failed
33	*runnable* check is a hard FAIL.  A check that genuinely needs an accelerator is
34	SKIPPED-silicon and listed at the end — never a false green.
35	"""
36	
37	from __future__ import annotations
38	
39	import argparse
40	import concurrent.futures
41	import dataclasses
42	import os
43	import re
44	import shutil
45	import subprocess
46	import sys
47	import threading
48	import time
49	from pathlib import Path
50	from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
51	
52	REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
53	
54	from grokking_optimizers import megakernel as mk
55	from grokking_optimizers import megakernel_codegen as cg
56	
57	OPTIMIZERS: Tuple[str, ...] = mk.OPTIMIZERS
58	MODELS: Tuple[str, ...] = mk.MODELS
59	ARCHES: Tuple[str, ...] = mk.MEGAKERNEL_ARCHS  # sm_90, gfx942, tpu_v6e
60	N_CELLS = len(OPTIMIZERS) * len(MODELS) * len(ARCHES)  # 99
61	
62	
63	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
64	# Result records
65	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
66	
67	PASS, FAIL, SKIP = "PASS", "FAIL", "SKIP-silicon"
68	
69	
70	@dataclasses.dataclass
71	class Check:
72	    phase: str
73	    name: str
74	    status: str            # PASS | FAIL | SKIP-silicon
75	    detail: str = ""
76	    seconds: float = 0.0
77	
78	
79	class Report:
80	    def __init__(self) -> None:
81	        self.checks: List[Check] = []
82	        self.tier_map: Dict[str, Dict[str, int]] = {}
83	        self.silicon: List[str] = []
84	        self.design: List[str] = []
85	
86	    def add(self, c: Check) -> Check:
87	        self.checks.append(c)
88	        glyph = {"PASS": "PASS ", "FAIL": "FAIL ",
89	                 "SKIP-silicon": "SKIP "}[c.status]
90	        tail = f"  ({c.seconds:.1f}s)" if c.seconds >= 0.1 else ""
91	        line = f"  {glyph} [{c.phase}] {c.name}{tail}"
92	        if c.detail and c.status != PASS:
93	            line += f"\n         {c.detail}"
94	        sys.stdout.write(line + "\n")
95	        sys.stdout.flush()
96	        return c
97	
98	    def count(self, status: str, phase: Optional[str] = None) -> int:
99	        return sum(1 for c in self.checks
100	                   if c.status == status and (phase is None or c.phase == phase))
101

"""scripts/fast_triage.py — FAST DIRECTIONAL "is this kernel change better or worse?"
triage for the SuperGrok1.5 perf inner loop.

WHY THIS EXISTS
  The campaign's rate-limiter is the ~20-30 min FULL cycle: rebuild the production
  `_ops` + the 3-seed fp64 PARITY HARD-GATE + A/A/A determinism + a d=2048 3-seed
  timing. That is the right arbiter for a KEEP — but it is far too slow to TRIAGE the
  dozens of candidate `-D SG_TUNED_*` macro-configs the hill-climb proposes. This
  harness gives a ~1-3 min directional signal so the expensive full cycle is reserved
  for the few candidates that survive triage.

  It is a THIN ORCHESTRATOR over the EXISTING machinery — it reinvents NOTHING. The
  --model switch selects which megakernel to triage (decoder DEFAULT | vit); both
  bench modules expose the SAME build_variant(profile=True)/measure(profile=True)->
  res["phase_cycles"] contract, and the relevance-gate logic is model-agnostic:
    * the per-variant build is `<bench>.build_variant(d, profile=True, …)` where <bench>
      is tuning.decoder_bench (mega_decoder_real_adamw_tc.cu) or tuning.vit_bench
      (mega_vit_real_adamw_tc.cu) — the coexisting bench TU built as a SEPARATELY-NAMED
      extension with its own torch-extensions build dir + ninja incremental rebuild +
      sccache. It is ONE cache-friendly TU, NOT the full `_ops`, and it NEVER touches
      the production `_ops.so` or the 33/33 gate.
    * the timing + per-phase clock64 read is `<bench>.measure(..., profile=True)`
      → `res["phase_cycles"]`, mapped by the model's phase table:
        decoder `decoder_bench.PHASE_NAMES` (8-slot g_dec_prof_max):
          [0]=P1_fwd [1]=P1_bwd [2]=B1_barrier [3]=P2_dW_GEMM
          [4]=P2_grad_asm [5]=P3_opt_tail [6]=B2_barrier [7]=B0_barrier
        vit `vit_bench.VIT_PHASE_NAMES` (6-slot g_vit_prof_max):
          [0]=P1_fwd [1]=P1_bwd [2]=B1_barrier [3]=P2_dW_GEMM
          [4]=P2_grad_asm [5]=P3_opt_tail
    * each variant is timed in its OWN worker subprocess (the tune_optimizers.py:645
      `subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-c", script])` idiom) so the baseline and the
      candidate get CLEAN, ISOLATED CUDA contexts — a wedged/OOM build of one variant
      cannot poison the other, and the warm context lives only as long as that variant.

PROFILING DOCTRINE  (measure broad · fix narrow · zoom deep only where you dig)
  * MEASURE BROAD, ALWAYS: every run reads ALL 8 phases in one clock64 shot. It is FREE
    (one read gets the whole step) and it is the ONLY way to stay honest — you cannot tell
    whether the phase you changed even MATTERS without every other phase as the denominator
    (its SHARE), and broad coverage is what catches the bottleneck MOVING (dW 60%->17% after
    the staging fix => the prize is now fwd/bwd). Never profile one phase alone and fix blind.

## 4. ABLATION / WIRING half — `phase4_ablation_matrix` (the NEW teeth)

The principle: **stub a function, rebuild a SHADOW `_ops`, run the cell gate; an
unchanged result means the function is dead/unwired → FAIL the ablation.** We need a
clean injection seam that (a) does not touch the production `_ops.so`, (b) does not
require editing every `.cu`, and (c) is honest (a real recompiled kernel, not a Python
mock).

### 4.1 The injection seam: `-D SG_ABLATE=<token>` (mirrors the existing `SG_TUNED_*`)

The codebase ALREADY compiles per-TU variants via `-D` macros
(`SG_TUNED_GEMM_IMPL`, fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:86; `SG_TUNED_MEGA_BLOCK`) and
already builds **separately-named shadow extensions** with their own
torch-extensions build dir + ninja incremental + sccache (`tuning/decoder_bench.py`
`build_variant`, described in scripts/fast_triage.py:1). **We reuse that exact
machinery.** The DRAFT adds one compile-time switch, defaulted OFF so production is
byte-identical:

DRAFT addition to `csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_components.cuh` (near the OptId enum,
opt_components.cuh:53), and the matching gate in `apply_optimizer` (:381):

```cpp
// ── PHASE-4 ABLATION SEAM (default OFF; production builds never define it). ──
// SG_ABLATE is a bitmask of phase IDs the harness NO-OPs to prove each phase is
// load-bearing. It is read ONLY inside the per-phase `if constexpr` arms, so an
// unset macro lowers to identical SASS (verified by the A/A/A check on a no-ABLATE
// build). Tokens mirror the kernel's own phase taxonomy.
#ifndef SG_ABLATE
#define SG_ABLATE 0
#endif
enum AblateBit : unsigned {
  ABL_NONE        = 0u,
  ABL_OPT_TAIL    = 1u<<0,  // P3 apply_optimizer<Opt>  -> skip the param update
  ABL_GRAD_CLIP   = 1u<<1,  // P2.5 global grad-norm clip -> force clip_coef=1
  ABL_PRODIGY_D   = 1u<<2,  // P2.6 d-reduce -> freeze d=d0
  ABL_MUON_NS     = 1u<<3,  // P2.7 Newton-Schulz -> skip orthogonalization (raw buf)
  ABL_SAM_2NDBWD  = 1u<<4,  // P2.4 SAM 2nd backward -> sam_dir=0 / sharpness=0
  ABL_SG_MU       = 1u<<5,  // P2.45 meta-net mu -> mu=0
  ABL_LAYERWISE_B1= 1u<<6,  // GrokAdamW per-tensor beta1 -> use global beta1
  ABL_NEURALGROK_PSI=1u<<7, // NeuralGrok psi amp -> g_amp=g (psi*alpha+beta=1)
  ABL_GROKFAST_COLDSTART=1u<<8, // Grokfast step-1 ema=grad seed -> ema=0
  ABL_SG2_SORT    = 1u<<9,  // SG2 segmented sort (STAGE -1) -> identity perm
};
```

Each phase's existing `if constexpr` arm gets a one-line guard, e.g. the GrokAdamW
cold-start at opt_components.cuh (the `if (step == 1) st.ema[idx] = grad[idx];` site,
opt_components.cuh in the Grokfast arm) becomes
`if (!(SG_ABLATE & ABL_GROKFAST_COLDSTART) && step == 1) st.ema[idx]=grad[idx];`. The
clip site in the P2.5 block guards `clip_coef` with `(SG_ABLATE & ABL_GRAD_CLIP)`. The
SAM 2nd-backward phase in `fused_*_megakernel.cuh` P2.4 is wrapped so the perturb→2nd
fwd+bwd is skipped and `sam_dir/sharpness` is written 0. This is **~12 one-line edits**,
all `#if`-inert in production.

WHY a macro and not a Python mock: the device functions are unreachable except through
the compiled kernel (the no-fallback contract, dispatch.py `has_kernels`:551). A real
recompiled-with-the-phase-removed kernel is the ONLY honest ablation — it proves the
phase's SASS is actually executed, not just present.

### 4.2 The ablation predicate

For ablation `A` targeting phase `φ` on cell `c`:
```
build shadow _ops with -DSG_ABLATE=<bit(φ)>           # ninja-incremental, own ext name
run run_cell_gate(c) against that shadow _ops          # same gate, no weakening
predicate: the gate's result MUST change in the DIRECTION the contract predicts:
   * a load-bearing phase  -> (1a)/(1b)/(1b-sam)/A-or-B FAILS, OR loss/grad/param
     moves beyond the gate tol vs the baseline shadow build (SG_ABLATE=0).
   * if the gate still PASSES bit-for-bit (== the SG_ABLATE=0 build) -> the phase
     produced NO observable effect -> DEAD/UNWIRED -> FLAG (the Phase-4 failure).
```

The **`SG_ABLATE=0` shadow build is the control** (must match production `_ops`
A/A/A — proves the macro is inert when unset). Every ablation is diffed against THAT
control, not against production, so the comparison isolates exactly the removed phase.

ablation has a **canonical witness cell** chosen so the phase is non-inert AND the

| ABL_PRODIGY_D | prodigy/decoder @ warm step ≥40 | d frozen at d0 ⇒ multistep parity diverges (the gate's own d-frozen control, gate:782) | P2.6 |
| ABL_MUON_NS | muon/decoder (pos[4,128]) | 2D params skip NS ⇒ (1a) 2D rel ≫ 2e-3 FAIL | P2.7; gate:408 |
| ABL_SAM_2NDBWD | looksam/decoder + /vit + /mamba | sam_dir≈0 ⇒ (1b-sam) FAIL (`g_sam_fp−g` is O(rho)≫0, gate:1222) | P2.4; gate:441 |
| ABL_SG_MU | supergrok11/decoder + supergrok15/decoder | mu=0 ⇒ (B) mu-vs-rescale·phi FAIL + (1a) tail diverges | P2.45; gate:466 |
| ABL_LAYERWISE_B1 | grokadamw/decoder | global β1 ⇒ (1b) m-rel ~0.895 FAIL (the documented signature, gate:341) | P3; gate:339 |
| ABL_NEURALGROK_PSI | neuralgrok/decoder | g_amp=g ⇒ (1b) m/v ≠ canonical psi-amp ref (gate:1235) | opt_components.cuh:250 |
| ABL_GROKFAST_COLDSTART | grokfast/decoder | ema=0 ⇒ ema slice rel ~50× off (gate:1358 documents this exact signature) | opt_components.cuh Grokfast arm |
| ABL_SG2_SORT | supergrok2/decoder | identity perm ⇒ SG2 (B1) vs fp64 oracle_step FAIL | sg2_stage_segmented_sort |

**Shared fwd/bwd + reduce ablation** is special: there is no "no-op the forward" that
leaves a meaningful gate. Instead its wiring is proven two ways already on silicon:
(i) the **A/A/A** check (gate:1409) is the reduce's determinism test — break the
ascending-CTA order (a one-line swap to a work-steal drain, the exact regression the
prodigy/mamba note describes, gate:782) and A/A/A FAILS; (ii) the **(1a) loss** matches
the fp64 oracle only if fwd/bwd ran. The harness adds ONE structural ablation,
`ABL_REDUCE_ORDER` (swap to atomic/work-steal reduce in the P2 block), whose witness is
`prodigy/decoder` A/A/A → must go from bit-exact to non-deterministic. That converts the
"is the deterministic reduce load-bearing" question into a silicon yes/no.

### 4.4 Dead-leaf detection for the GEMM/dW leaf helpers

The leaf `*_gemm_fwd` / `*_dw_run_tile` / `*_attn_*_tile` functions are too fine for a
per-leaf ablation macro. They are covered transitively: ablating the *phase* they belong
to (the forward tile, the dW assembly) is caught by (1a) loss / grad. For provably-dead
leaf detection the harness leans on the **build-level signal** instead of a runtime
ablation: a `nvcc -Xptxas -v` / `cuobjdump -sass` symbol-presence pass over the shadow
TU (the `tuning/decoder_bench.py` build already emits the object) — a `__device__`
function that is defined but whose symbol is fully inlined-away AND unreferenced in the
SASS is flagged for the Phase-5 dead-code task, not failed here (it may be a legitimately
inlined helper). This keeps Phase-4 honest about what it can prove at runtime vs what is
a static-analysis hand-off to Phase 5.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. Driving it 8-GPU-wide

The work is **embarrassingly parallel across (cell, ablation)** and the only shared
mutable resource is the compiled shadow `_ops` per `SG_ABLATE` token — which is keyed by
the macro value, so each ablation token gets its OWN named extension build dir (exactly
the `build_variant` idiom, fast_triage.py:1). Plan:

### 5.1 Unit of work
A **job** = `(cell_key, ablate_token)`. Isolation jobs use `ablate_token=0` (control).
Total ≈ 33 isolation cells × 4 seeds (≈132) + ~12 ablation witnesses × (1 ablated + share
the control) ≈ ~150 gate invocations + ~12 shadow builds. The builds (sccache-warm
ninja-incremental) dominate; gate runs are ~1-2 min each.

### 5.2 GPU assignment (reuse the existing isolation pattern)
The gate ALREADY runs each contamination-prone cell in a **fresh subprocess** via the
`--cell` CLI (`_run_cell_gate_subprocess`, gate:1433, sets `PYTHONPATH`, asserts
returncode + "=> PASS" + "1/1 cells passed"). The harness generalizes that to a pool:

```
DRAFT: scripts/phase4_runner.py
  --gpus 0-7  --jobs <list of (cell, ablate_token)>  --build-root .phase4/builds
  for each ablate_token: build ONE shadow _ops (-DSG_ABLATE=token) into
     .phase4/builds/abl_<token>/  (ninja-incremental, sccache; serialize the BUILDS,
     parallelize the RUNS — a build pins a GPU only for its arch probe).
  schedule jobs over 8 workers; worker i sets CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=i and runs
     PYTHONPATH=<build_root/abl_token>:. python -m tests.hw.test_l3tc_tail_gate --cell <cell>
     in a subprocess (the EXISTING CLI — no gate code duplicated). For the SG2 /
     contamination cells it already self-isolates further (gate:1466).
```

Concretely the scheduler is the same `concurrent.futures` pool `verify_all` uses
(verify_all.py:40 imports `concurrent.futures`, `--jobs N`, verify_all.py:30). We do NOT
write a new scheduler — we point `verify_all`'s pool at a job list of subprocess
invocations, each pinned to a GPU by `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`.

### 5.3 Why a subprocess per job (not one process, many devices)
- The `_ops` extension caches arch detection (`detect_arch` `lru_cache`, dispatch.py:266;
  C++ `static const int cached_arch`, dispatch.cpp:147) — one process cannot switch the
  ablation token, because the imported `_ops` is fixed at first import. A subprocess with
  a different `PYTHONPATH` (pointing at a different shadow build) is the clean boundary.
- The #19d device-global contamination (gate:47-63) is ALREADY handled by the subprocess
  isolation; spreading across GPUs only strengthens it (no shared device state).

### 5.4 Aggregation
Each worker emits the gate's structured verdict (it already prints `(1a)/(1b)/(2)` lines
and exits 0/1). `phase4_runner.py` collects `{(cell, token): (passed, verdict_lines)}`
and applies the **Section 4.2 predicate**: isolation jobs must PASS; ablation jobs must
FLIP (control-PASS → ablated-FAIL). The deliverable is one table:
`results/h100_grokking_race/phase4_verify.json` (mirrors wiring_check.json,
wiring_check.py:34) + a markdown summary with, per function: `isolated=PASS/FAIL`,
`ablation=LOAD-BEARING / DEAD-UNWIRED`.

### 5.5 gfx942 / tpu preserved
`phase4_runner.py` is `arch == 90`-gated at entry (it forces `FORCE_ARCH=sm_90` only when
on a Hopper host; on gfx942 it SKIPs the wgmma shadow builds and instead runs the
existing gfx942 `verify_all --phase 3` + `check_math_single_source` — those are the AMD
composition gates and are untouched). The `SG_ABLATE` macro is added to the sm_90 headers
only; the gfx942 `.hip` tree and `opt_components.hip.hpp` are NOT edited (the macro is
absent there, so `#ifndef SG_ABLATE / #define SG_ABLATE 0` keeps them compiling
unchanged). TPU stays Python/JAX (dispatch.cpp:39 rejects TPU at the C++ boundary; the
harness never reaches it).

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 6. What the lead actually applies (files + regions)

NEW files (driver + unit; no production behavior change):
- `scripts/phase4_runner.py` — the 8-GPU scheduler (thin wrapper over the `--cell` CLI +
  `concurrent.futures`, mirrors `_run_cell_gate_subprocess` gate:1433 and
  `verify_all` pool).
- `tests/hw/phase4_isolation_matrix.py` — the ISO registry (Section 3) + CPU units
  `scalars_roundtrip` / `routing_table` / `driver_edges` (assert the Python-surface
  mappings with no GPU).
- `tests/hw/phase4_ablation_matrix.py` — the ABLATE registry (Section 4.3) + the
  control-vs-ablated predicate; calls into the shadow builds.

MINIMAL edits to EXISTING files (all `#if`-inert when `SG_ABLATE`/`--ablate` unset):
- `csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_components.cuh:53` — add the `AblateBit` enum + `#ifndef
  SG_ABLATE` default; guard the Grokfast cold-start, GrokAdamW layer-wise-β1,
  NeuralGrok psi, and the `apply_optimizer` opt-tail with the matching bit (~6 lines).
- `csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh` (P2.4 SAM block, P2.5 clip,
  P2.6 d-reduce, P2 reduce-order) — and the vit/mamba twins
  `fused_vit_megakernel.cuh` / `fused_mamba_megakernel.cuh` — one `if (SG_ABLATE & …)`
  guard per phase (~6 lines each, mechanically mirrored).
- `csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_stages_precompute.cuh` (P2.7 muon NS, P2.45 SG mu) — guard the
  stage body (~3 lines).
- `csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh` (`sg2_stage_segmented_sort`) — identity-perm
  guard (~2 lines).
- `tuning/decoder_bench.py` / `vit_bench.py` / a mamba twin — accept an `ablate_token`
  kwarg that appends `-DSG_ABLATE=<token>` to the existing `extra_cuda_cflags`
  (the `build_variant` already threads `-D` flags; ~2 lines).
- `grokking_optimizers/verify_all.py` — register a new `phase4` entry-point that shells to
  `scripts/phase4_runner.py` so `verify_all --phase 4silicon` surfaces it in the unified
  report (optional; ~10 lines, keeps one front door).

NO edits to: `csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h` (single source — the drift guard forbids it),
`dispatch.cpp` (the ABI is unchanged; ablation is a kernel-body switch, not an ABI arg),
the gfx942/tpu trees, the production `_ops` build (the macro defaults to 0).

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 7. Honesty / limits (so the lead can vet)

- The ablation predicate is **"the gate changes"**, which inherits the gate's own
  blind-spots: a single-step gate is BLIND to step-1-inert mechanisms (clip, prodigy-d,
  SG2 CSA fidelity — all documented at gate:341/371/528). The harness therefore drives
  the **multistep** witnesses (gate already has `_multistep_grokadamw_parity` /
  `_prodigy_multistep_parity` / `--sg11-warmup`) for exactly those ablations, NOT the
  step-1 gate. Listed per-row in 4.3.
- A phase that is genuinely a no-op at step 1 AND has no multistep witness wired
  (none currently — every staged opt has one) would be UN-ablatable; the harness FLAGS
  "no decisive witness" rather than silently passing it.
- Leaf GEMM/dW helpers get **phase-level** ablation + a **static SASS-presence** hand-off
  to Phase 5, not a per-leaf runtime ablation (Section 4.4) — stated plainly so no false
  "every leaf silicon-ablated" claim is made.
- The `SG_ABLATE=0` control build MUST be byte-A/A/A-identical to production `_ops`; if it
  is not, the macro insertion itself perturbed codegen and the whole ablation set is
  void — that equality is the harness's first assertion.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 8. Run recipe (deliverable)

```
# isolation + ablation, 8 GPUs, full sm_90 surface:
PYTHONPATH=. FORCE_ARCH=sm_90 python scripts/phase4_runner.py \
    --gpus 0-7 --seeds 42,7,123,999 --build-root .phase4/builds \
    --out results/h100_grokking_race/phase4_verify.json
# CPU-only Python-surface units (no GPU needed):
PYTHONPATH=. python -m tests.hw.phase4_isolation_matrix --cpu-units
# single function, debug:
PYTHONPATH=. python scripts/phase4_runner.py --only ABL_SAM_2NDBWD:looksam/decoder
```
Exit 0 iff: every ISO node maps to a live gate AND its gate PASSED at all seeds; every
ablation witness FLIPPED control-PASS→ablated-FAIL (no dead/unwired phase); the
`SG_ABLATE=0` control == production A/A/A.
